Howard Johnson
Howard Johnson is a virtuoso on the tuba, baritone saxophone, and pennywhistle, and has collaborated with Gil Evans, the “Saturday Night Live”
band, and John Lennon, among many others. Howard directed and recorded with Gravity, his own innovative ensemble that included four tubas.
Howard was interviewed in New York City on January 14, 2019 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
I said I didn’t know what to expect coming to Texas Christian because I didn’t know if I’d be able to cuss or not.
And did you?
And the tuba teacher says, “Shit yes.”
Well let’s get started. My name is Monk Rowe and I’m privileged to be in the home of Howard Johnson today. Thank you for allowing us to come and chat with you.
Well thank you for inviting me.
I picture you going to a gig somewhere in Manhattan or New York and moving your tuba and your baritone saxophone and I wonder what that was like.
You mean transporting?
Transporting.
I’ve been doing it since I was about 14 so it never seemed like that much of a task until I got in my present condition which is fairly out of whack.
You just figured out how to deal with it.
Yeah. But I think it contributed to me being out of whack.
Yeah that’s a very physical — people don’t think about the physical end of playing gigs and especially if you’ve got the low end thing happening.

Well you know a lot of people do think about it, they wonder if I wish I’d played the flute. To which I say the flute? I’m going to want to play the flute when I can do what I do with my instruments? I’m going to be happy playing a flute?
I guess so.
I don’t think so.

And when you say what I can do with your instruments I wanted to share with you you’re written up in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz and they said that, “You rediscovered the idea of the tuba as a solo instrument despite its cumbersome nature.” So I think I can agree with that when I listen to some of the tuba work you’ve done. And at the other end you’ve got the high end covered with the pennywhistle too?
